answer.exemplar: The centre of the locus is the midpoint of the two ledges, since that is the point which is symmetric between them. The constant total distance equals twice the semi-major axis, so halving the stated sum gives a. The distance from the centre to either ledge is the focal distance c, and the semi-minor axis then follows from b squared equal to a squared minus c squared. Together a, b and the orientation of the ledge line describe the whole ellipse.

questions.explanation: The centre is the midpoint of the two foci and the constant sum equals twice the semi-major axis. The focal distance c then gives the semi-minor axis.
questions.hint: Midpoint for the centre, half the sum for a.

answer.exemplar: The constant sum of the two distances is twice the semi-major axis, so halving it gives a. The two pegs are the foci, so the distance from the midpoint of the pegs to either peg is the focal distance c. questions.learningObjective: Explain how secant products let a survey find an unknown length
questions.stem: A survey team uses two secants from a stake outside a circular pond to find a missing distance. Explain how the four measured lengths are related and how the unknown one is recovered.

answer.exemplar: Every secant drawn from the same external point carries the same product of its near and far segments, and that product is the power of the point with respect to the circle.
